page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture, configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 32 GB of system memory. It is powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 7B13 processors executing 2 threads per core. The memory allocation yields 4 GB of RAM per vCPU, maintaining a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. The processor architecture includes 32 KB of L1 data cache per core, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, backed by instruction flags including AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, but without AVX-512 extensions.

Performance metrics reflect consistent mid-tier execution with standout single-thread compute. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 2691.89, placing it in the top 25% of evaluated systems. Multi-core performance sits in the middle 50%, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 10798.81 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5419.0. Memory bandwidth reaches 514.76 GB/sec for small cached reads and 45.33 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB blocks. However, parallel compression shows limitations, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression recording 27.85 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 25%.

The n2d-standard-8 carries no bundled local storage and includes zero GPUs, requiring reliance on remote persistent disk volumes for storage throughput. Its balanced hardware profile provides predictable resource allocation without the overhead of specialized hardware. Delivering 8.25 GB/sec static web throughput and 8.04 million Redis SET operations per second, this instance is suited for web serving, containerized microservices, build pipelines, and relational database workloads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine provisioned with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM on an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7B13 processor. Operating across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, it delivers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio alongside 32 MB of shared L3 cache. The instance features no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, relying on external network-attached storage. Benchmark testing highlights upper-quartile single-core throughput in stress-ng tests, coupled with solid middle-tier results across Geekbench multi-core workloads, memory bandwidth tests, and Redis key-value operations. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression ranks in the lower quartile. With balanced compute resources and reliable static web throughput of 8.25 GB/sec, the n2d-standard-8 serves standard application tiers, microservice clusters, development environments, and moderate database deployments.
